text:
[Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) directly addresses sampled-softmax bias: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its revised derivation applies importance sampling to negatives and introduces a stop-gradient uncertainty weight. This is sampling-bias correction, not false-negative detection. [Sampled Estimators For Softmax Must Be Biased (NeurIPS 2025)](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/42b7c2f6d320d1fe1afa899a6319d6d7-Abstract-Conference.html) establishes that subset-only softmax estimators remain biased; correction should be viewed as bias reduction.

For harder discrimination, [Scalable Cross-Entropy (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721) selectively computes informative catalog logits using GPU-efficient operations. Earlier, directly relevant [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) treats sampled false negatives as useful training information rather than indiscriminately suppressing them. [Hard vs. Noise (AAAI 2026)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/38605) distinguishes hard negatives from noisy potential positives using LLM-derived relevance, but its pretrained semantic machinery is unsuitable under this task’s restrictions.

Practical hypothesis for the existing single BERT4Rec: compare corrected sampled softmax with a conservative stochastic hard-negative curriculum, retaining uniform sampling and excluding known training positives. Use the actual proposal probabilities for correction; deterministic top-score selection cannot simply inherit uniform logQ. Treat confidence-based filtering as a heuristic because high scores alone cannot identify false negatives. Preserve masked-target training and appended-mask inference. Select using fixed four-category macro validation HR@10; improved training margins do not establish generalization or guarantee gains in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics.
